## Longeveron Announces Updated Results from ELPIS II Phase 2b Clinical Trial Evaluating Laromestrocel as a Potential Treatment for Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS)


10.26.26


[Download (opens in new window) PDF 160 KB](https://s25.q4cdn.com/509659455/files/doc_news/Longeveron-Announces-Updated-Results-from-ELPIS-II-Phase-2b-Clinical-Trial-Evaluating-Laromestrocel-as-a-Potential-Treatment-for-Hypo-UUG52.pdf)


Important Secondary Clinical Outcome Endpoint MACE Achieved Statistical Significance


**ELPIS II 2 Data in HLHS Selected for Late-Breaking Science Program Podium Presentation in the American Heart Association’s (AHA) 2026 Scientific Sessions**


- *As previously reported, the ELPIS II trial did not meet the primary endpoint of increase in right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) at month 12 and the Company planned to continue analysis of additional data*
- *Additional analysis demonstrates an important pre-specified secondary clinical outcome endpoint, major adverse cardiac events (MACE), achieved statistical significance with 8 events in the standard of care arm versus 1 in the laromestrocel treatment arm (P=0.043)*
- *Laromestrocel was associated with fewer adjudicated clinical and safety events than the standard of care arm*
- *The Company believes the results suggest that laromestrocel may have the potential to meaningfully improve clinical outcomes of children with HLHS undergoing Stage II surgical palliation*


MIAMI, Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --[Longeveron Inc.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=eyRK0MD0NHuOy4TBiKA2DPJkaTEVbKVK_a0aC98L7h2UxUrjVcjbgdi97bxcFOcfHnFV5HcKBjSnk_nFiomB1TsIVZGd-0mSjOiDMp7vOg8=) (NASDAQ: LGVN), a clinical stage biotechnology company developing cellular therapy for life-threatening, rare pediatric and chronic aging-related conditions, today announced updated results from ELPIS II following planned additional analysis conducted by the Company and the National Institutes of Health (NIH) funded trial investigators. ELPIS II is the Company’s Phase 2b clinical trial evaluating its investigational stem cell therapy laromestrocel as an adjunct to Stage 2 palliative surgery in 40 infants with hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS).


The ELPIS II trial did not meet the primary efficacy endpoint of change from baseline in right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) at Month 12. Based on the secondary endpoints, laromestrocel was associated with fewer adjudicated clinical and safety events than the standard of care (SOC) arm. Additional review of the pre-specified secondary endpoint major adverse cardiac events (MACE) showed statistical significance with 8 events in the SOC arm versus 1 in the laromestrocel treatment arm (P=0.043). Laromestrocel demonstrated a favorable safety and tolerability profile through 12 months, with no treatment-related serious adverse events identified. The Company believes the favorable pre-specified secondary endpoint findings suggest that laromestrocel has the potential to meaningfully improve clinical outcomes of children with HLHS undergoing Stage II surgical palliation. The Company intends to request a meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to review the results to determine potential next steps for the HLHS development program.


**Results**
Among the 40 randomized infants in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population, baseline and Month 12 cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) were available for 28 infants (15-S0C, 13- Laromestrocel group). Mean RVEF decreased by 2.6(SD=10.5) percentage points in the SoC group and 3.3 (SD=8.4) percentage points in the Laromestrocel group, with no statistically significant difference between 2 groups (baseline adjusted difference=-1.36, 95% CI: -8.0 - 6.7, p=0.68).

**American Heart Association’s (AHA) 2026 Scientific Sessions**
The Phase 2 data from the ELPIS II trial have been selected for a Late-Breaking Science Program podium presentation at the[American Heart Association’s (AHA) 2026 Scientific Sessions](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=a0WaAeFeecDXyotcg4KOEkaWYKtvNsjR3bMN0Qhch_Luuo3JbAhpwGB6AgT-viEszFKI83XKEZqopA-8-Ot6o1JWuIowbfZrCPR3ygldb7aluElGiCXPNIJC8pPQR98oF-fg6yZZB6cqA3ljhse47wzPi8mJ3FeXuJQHBnx_z68=) which will take place in Chicago on November 6-9, 2026.


**Presentation**


**Date:** Sunday, November 8, 2026


**Time:** 10:10am CDT


**Session:** Featured Science, FS.07, Heart Failure Care for Novel Phenotypes


**Title:** ELPIS II: A Phase 2b Randomized Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Laromestrocel as Adjunct Therapy During Stage II Palliation for Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome


**About ELPIS II**
ELPIS II is an investigational Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind, multicenter, two-arm trial conducted by Longeveron in collaboration with the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) through grants from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) ([ClinicalTrials.gov](http://clinicaltrials.gov/) : NCT04925024). A total of 40 infants with HLHS were randomized 1:1 to receive a single intramyocardial dose of an investigational drug called laromestrocel that was administered during Stage 2 palliative surgery (bidirectional Glenn or hemi-Fontan procedure) or standard of care surgery alone, and were followed for 12 months. Long-term follow-up for transplant-free survival is planned for up to 5 years.


The trial’s primary endpoint was the difference between groups’ change from baseline in RVEF at 12 months, assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). As previously disclosed, FDA has advised Longeveron that RVEF alone would not be sufficient to demonstrate efficacy for regulatory approval.


Research reported in this press release was supported by the National Heart, Lung, And Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health under Award Number UH3HL148318. The content is solely the responsibility of the Company and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health.


**About Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS)**
HLHS is a rare congenital heart defect that affects approximately 1,000 infants per year in the U.S. Infants with HLHS are born with an underdeveloped left ventricle, which creates a life-threatening condition due to the heart’s inability to pump adequate amounts of blood throughout the body. The current treatment requires infants to undergo a complex three-stage heart reconstruction surgery process over the first five years of their life. Despite staged surgical palliation, long-term mortality and morbidity remain substantial, with progressive right ventricular dysfunction representing a major contributor to adverse outcomes. There is clearly an important unmet medical need to improve right ventricular function in these infants to positively impact both short- and long-term patient outcomes.


**About laromestrocel (Lomecel-B®)**
Laromestrocel is an investigational living cell product made from specialized cells isolated from the bone marrow of young, healthy adult donors. These specialized cells, known as mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), are essential to the human endogenous biological repair mechanism. MSCs have the potential to perform a number of complex functions in the body and possibly support tissue repair and regenerative signaling pathways. They also may respond to sites of injury or disease and may secrete bioactive factors that are immunomodulatory and regenerative. We believe laromestrocel MSCs may have multiple potential mechanisms of action that may lead to anti-inflammatory, anti-fibrotic, and/or pro-vascular regenerative responses, and therefore may have broad applicability for a range of rare and aging related diseases.


**About Longeveron Inc.** Longeveron is a clinical stage biotechnology company developing regenerative medicines to address unmet medical needs. The Company’s lead investigational product is laromestrocel (Lomecel-B®), an allogeneic mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy product isolated from the bone marrow of young, healthy adult donors. We believe laromestrocel has multiple potential mechanisms of action encompassing pro-vascular, pro-regenerative, anti-inflammatory, and tissue repair and healing effects with broad potential applications across a spectrum of disease areas. Laromestrocel development programs have received five distinct and important FDA designations: for the HLHS program - Orphan Drug designation, Fast Track designation, and Rare Pediatric Disease designation; and, for the AD program - Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designation and Fast Track designation.
